_comment: Fit controller: one foldable box, laid out as compactly as the hand-drawn fittingWidget.ui it replaces. The actions come first and stay big; the two fields a fit is driven by day to day (Steps, Runs) stay inline; everything that is configuration -- which sampler, thinning, chunking, chi2 cutoff, chain format, optimiser tolerances -- lives behind the settings button, in optimization_settings.view.json, and is written to the user settings.

buttons.label: ▶  Fit
buttons.description: Run the optimiser on the selected fit.

buttons.label: Sample
buttons.description: Sample the posterior of the free parameters. Writes the chains, the diagnostics and the project to a folder.
Sampling and fitting settings: which sampler, thinning, chunk size, χ² cutoff, chain format and the optimiser tolerances. Saved to your settings.

buttons.label: auto
buttons.description: Choose the fit range from the data: the rising edge to where the signal reaches the background.
Attach a different dataset to this fit.

sections.label: Dataset
sections.description: Which fit of this window the controls act on.

sections.label: Result
sections.description: Which stored result of this fit is shown.

sections.label: First
sections.description: First channel included in the fit.

sections.label: Last
sections.description: Last channel included in the fit.

sections.label: First (2)
sections.description: First channel of the second axis, for two-dimensional data.

sections.label: Last (2)
sections.description: Last channel of the second axis, for two-dimensional data.

sections.label: Steps
sections.description: Sampling steps per walker, in thousands. The diagnostics report whether it was enough.

sections.label: Runs
sections.description: Independent sampling runs. Their disagreement is the R-hat that says whether the chain converged, so more than one is the point.

sections.label: Local first
sections.description: Optimise each dataset on its own before the global fit, which usually starts the global step much closer to the optimum.
